Priya: FYI I'm opening a PR to consolidate troubleshooting steps for 429s/timeouts/context-clips into one compact runbook + quick SDK examples. want a short "how to repro" section too.
Owen: 👍 can we include a tiny golang snippet? ops asked for a typed example they can drop into services.
Priya: sure. plan: runbook (runbooks/429-and-context-guidance.md), sdk examples (sdk-snippets/go/fallback_trim.md, sdk-snippets/python/fallback_trim.md), and a test harness under tools/rate-sim. PR link when ready.
Tara: echo on the harness. I can add a Docker compose that injects 429s at a controlled rate so QA can validate both trimming and fallback behavior. Make sure it also captures request_ids and token counts.
Ben: small copy note: don't advise automatic fallback to smaller models by default. recommend telemetry + canary first.
Priya: agreed — will add rollout checklist, telemetry events to emit (trim_applied, fallback_model, original_token_count, trimmed_token_count), and a feature-flag example.
Owen: here's a tiny Go example for trimming + fallback (pseudo):
```go
// keep suffix up to maxTokens, then retry on 429 using smaller model
func GenerateWithTrim(client *Client, prompt string) (string, error) {
    out, err := client.Generate(context.Background(), prompt)
    if err == nil {
        return out, nil
    }
    if IsTooManyRequests(err) {
        trimmed := TrimSuffixByTokens(prompt, 800) // keep last 800 tokens
        return client.GenerateWithModel(context.Background(), trimmed, "redwood-small")
    }
    return "", err
}
```
Tara: nice. for python I'll add an example that shows an exponential backoff + trim-on-fallback pattern.
Priya: add a short section on token accounting: link to `utils/token-counter` and show cli: `./tools/token-count --text "..."`. emphasize trimming from the front unless the user needs the prefix.
Ben: include a troubleshooting checklist at top: 1) verify client token estimates 2) reproduce with local harness 3) enable trimmed fallback behind flag 4) collect telemetry + contact infra if persistent 429s.
Tara: QA will need a tiny synthetic script that alternates 200 and 429 responses to validate exponential backoff jitter. I'll push the compose + small python replay script under `tools/rate-sim`.
Priya: one more: mention context-window errors (400-range) separately from 429s; show example message to detect: "context length exceeded" vs HTTP 429.
Owen: small lint: use lower-case filenames in sdk-snippets (we already do).
Docs Bot: PR drafted by Priya 14 https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4987 (draft).
Ben: assigning reviewers: Owen + Tara. I'll add infra oncall as optional reviewer for escalations section.
Priya: action list added in PR description. tagging for follow-up next week. :rocket:
